severity_levels.blocker: map or sector will not load, or loads with a game-breaking absence (no collision)
severity_levels.major: loads but is visibly or functionally broken to a player
severity_levels.info: occurs in shipped official data; report, never fail the build

rules.symptom: Client refuses the map; player is bounced to the login screen or the map never appears.
rules.checks: setting.txt exists and carries all six required keys with ScriptType == MapSetting.
rules.predicate: File exists AND lowercased key set contains {scripttype, cellscale, heightscale, viewradius, mapsize, textureset} AND scripttype's first token lowercases to 'mapsetting'.
rules.fix: Emit all six. Write CellScale 200, HeightScale 0.500000, ViewRadius 128 verbatim — the WorldEditor normalises those three from constants on every save.
rules.corpus: 3 of 142 maps have no setting.txt (metin2_guild_village_01/02/03); they are stubs with only mapproperty.txt.

rules.symptom: A whole row or column of the map is invisible and unreachable; server and client disagree about where the map ends.
rules.checks: No sector folder lies outside the MapSize rectangle.
rules.predicate: For every folder matching ^\d{6}$: int(name[0:3]) < MapSizeX AND int(name[3:6]) < MapSizeY.
rules.fix: Raise MapSize to cover the real extent, or delete the surplus folders.
rules.corpus: 2 violations: metin2_map_devilscatacomb (MapSize 7x7, 54 folders, max (6,7)); metin2_map_trent02 (MapSize 3x3, 16 folders forming 4x4, max (3,3)).

rules.symptom: Empty holes in the world where sectors are declared but absent.
rules.checks: Sector folder count versus MapSizeX * MapSizeY.
rules.predicate: len(sector_folders) == MapSizeX * MapSizeY. Report the delta; never fail.
rules.fix: None needed — the client renders nothing there. Merge output is legitimately sparse when the quadrant inputs differ in size.
rules.corpus: 7 maps are sparse. metin2_map_smhgate_a1/b1/c1 declare 4x5=20 and ship 3 sectors; smhgate_b1's sectors start at x=2, so the grid need not touch the origin.

rules.symptom: Minimap and world map are offset from where the player actually is; server sector ids do not line up.
rules.checks: BasePosition alignment, and agreement with atlasinfo.txt.
rules.predicate: baseX % 6400 == 0 AND baseY % 6400 == 0 (error) ; baseX % 25600 == 0 AND baseY % 25600 == 0 (warning) ; atlasinfo row for this map == (baseX, baseY, MapSizeX, MapSizeY).
rules.fix: Snap BasePosition to a multiple of 25600 and rewrite atlasinfo.txt to match.
rules.corpus: 4 maps are 6400-aligned but not 25600-aligned: gm_guild_build (83200,0), metin2_map_t2 (6400,0), metin2_map_t3 (32000,0), metin2_map_t4 (57600,0). All are guild/instance maps.

rules.symptom: A sector's terrain, objects and collision are all absent even though its binaries are on disk.
rules.checks: Every XXXYYY folder has areaproperty.txt with ScriptType AreaProperty.
rules.predicate: File exists AND its scripttype token lowercases to 'areaproperty'. LoadTerrain never reaches height.raw/tile.raw without it.
rules.fix: Write a 3-key file: ScriptType AreaProperty / AreaName "" / NumWater <n>.
rules.corpus: 2 violations: metin2_map_boss_awaken_skipia/000000 and metin2_map_boss_crack_skipia/000000 contain only attr.atr, while both maps declare MapSize 6 6.

rules.symptom: An audit that whitelists filenames rejects official sectors.
rules.checks: Unknown files present in a sector folder.
rules.predicate: Filename not in the documented set. Do NOT fail on: minimap_{top,bottom,left,right,lefttop,righttop,leftbottom,rightbottom}.dds, height.tga, contents.obv.
rules.fix: Copy unknown files through verbatim on merge/reskin.
rules.corpus: minimap_*.dds in ~70 sectors (all metin2_map_eastplain_0*); height.tga in 39 (metin2_map_b1 etc.); contents.obv in 29 (metin2_map_elemental_0*). None are documented in the spec.

rules.symptom: Terrain in one sector is garbage — random spikes, wrapped rows, or a shifted grid.
rules.checks: height.raw is exactly 34322 bytes.
rules.predicate: size == 131*131*2 == 34322. The loader is a blind memcpy with NO size validation, so a wrong size fails silently at runtime.
rules.fix: Write exactly 34322 bytes: uint16 LE, row-major, index [(sy+1)*131 + (sx+1)] for logical vertex (sx,sy) in [-1,129].
rules.corpus: 0 violations in 1341 height.raw files.

rules.symptom: A visible crack, step or lighting seam along a sector border.
rules.checks: Shared edge vertices agree between adjacent sectors (the 1-sample skirt).
rules.fix: After any height edit, mirror the shared vertex row/column into every adjacent sector's skirt.
rules.corpus: Measured over all 972 E-W adjacent pairs: 934 match exactly, 38 mismatch (96% conformance). Worst: metin2_guild_war4 000000|001000 (13/129 differ), metin2_map_a3 001003|002003 (7), metin2_map_b3 000003|001003 (6). Treat as major in generated output, info when auditing shipped maps.

rules.symptom: A sector is dead flat — often an untouched sector nobody edited.
rules.checks: height.raw has a single distinct value.
rules.predicate: len(set(u16 values)) == 1. Escalate to minor when the constant is exactly 32767 (the NewHeightMap default fill).
rules.fix: None if intentional (indoor/dungeon floors are flat).
rules.corpus: 101 flat sectors. Constants seen: 32767 x35 (untouched default), 32646 x35, 32752 x22, 32614 x3, 30770 x2, 0 x4.

rules.symptom: Player falls through the world or spawns at the absolute bottom; objects float 160 m above the ground.
rules.checks: Raw height 0 present (worldZ 0).
rules.predicate: min(u16 values) == 0. Escalate when the whole sector is 0.
rules.fix: Raise the terrain to the map's working band (official maps sit around raw 16000-20000, i.e. worldZ 8000-10000 cm).
rules.corpus: 96 sectors contain a raw 0. Four are entirely zero: metin2_map_elemental_01/000002, metin2_map_elemental_01/004003, metin2_map_elemental_03/004003, metin2_map_elemental_03/004004.

rules.symptom: A terrain spike shooting to the sky, or an implausibly steep cliff.
rules.checks: Height extremes and per-sector relief.
rules.predicate: max(u16) == 65535 (top of the representable range, worldZ 32767.5 cm) — minor. max-min > 40000 raw (200 m of relief inside a 256 m sector) — info.
rules.fix: Clamp the generator's height output; check for unsigned wrap.
rules.corpus: 6 sectors contain 65535: metin2_map_mt_thunder/000001, /001003, metin2_map_smhgate_devils/000001, metin2_map_t1/000000, metin2_map_whitdragonvalley/000002, /002000. 80 sectors exceed the 40000 relief threshold, so that half is info-only.

rules.symptom: Ground textures are shifted, sheared, or the sector's texture layout is scrambled.
rules.checks: tile.raw is exactly 66564 bytes.
rules.predicate: size == 258*258 == 66564. Blind memcpy on load, no validation. Tolerate size >= 66564 when READING (ignore the tail); always write exactly 66564.
rules.fix: Truncate or pad to 66564.
rules.corpus: 1 violation in 1341: gm_guild_build/000000/tile.raw is 66567 bytes (3 trailing bytes). The engine ignores them; strict tools blank the layer.

rules.symptom: Bright pink / checkerboard error texture on patches of ground.
rules.checks: Every tile index is within the TextureSet's TextureCount.
rules.predicate: For every one of the 66564 bytes v: v <= TextureCount. (v == 0 is the eraser and always legal.)
rules.fix: Repaint the offending tiles, or extend the TextureSet.
rules.corpus: 47 sectors ship this way: metin2_12zi_stage uses index 32 against metin2_12temple.txt count 23; metin2_guild_village uses 7 against count 6; metin2_map_b1 uses 19 against metin2_B1.txt count 17. Warn, do not hard-fail, when auditing official maps.

rules.symptom: Untextured black or void patches in the ground.
rules.checks: Eraser (index 0) tiles inside the visible grid.
rules.predicate: count of raw[(ty+1)*258 + (tx+1)] == 0 for tx,ty in 0..255. Border bytes being 0 is harmless — exclude them.
rules.fix: Paint a base layer under the whole sector; the splat loop starts at index 1 and never draws index 0.
rules.corpus: 39 sectors have eraser tiles in the inner grid; metin2_map_devilscatacomb has 765 per sector across 8 sectors (deliberate — indoor catacomb).

rules.symptom: Texture blending stops abruptly at a sector border.
rules.checks: tile.raw 1-tile skirt agrees with the neighbour's edge column/row.
rules.fix: Mirror edge tiles into the neighbour's border on paint.
rules.corpus: MUST STAY INFO. Over the same 972 adjacent pairs: 522 match, 450 mismatch (46%). The WorldEditor does not reliably mirror tile borders and the maps look fine. Only the inner grid is worth asserting.

rules.symptom: Error texture on ground whose tile index looks perfectly in range.
rules.checks: The TextureSet has no missing or duplicated Texture%03d slot.
rules.predicate: Parse block names with /^\s*Start\s+Texture(\d+)\s*$/i into a SET of slot numbers (never a positional list). Assert slots == {1..TextureCount} and no slot number repeats. Then assert every tile byte v satisfies v == 0 or v in slots.
rules.fix: Rewrite the TextureSet as a dense Texture001..TextureN run.
rules.corpus: 3 shipped texturesets are malformed and 2 are in active use. metin2_guild_village.txt: TextureCount 6, blocks Texture002..006 — slot 1 MISSING. metin2_BayBlackSand.txt: TextureCount 11, blocks 001,002,004..011 — slot 3 MISSING, and 9 sectors of metin2_map_bayblacksand paint index 3. metin2_map_naga1.txt: TextureCount 14 with 15 blocks — Texture012 appears twice.
rules.generator_note: This is the input that breaks positional textureset parsers. MapForge's parseTextureSet assigns slot idx+1 by file position; for guild_village and BayBlackSand that is off by one for every entry after the hole, so a merge/reskin shifts every tile on the map by one texture. Key the remap on the parsed block number.

rules.symptom: Every ground tile on the map is the error texture.
rules.checks: The setting.txt TextureSet reference resolves to an actual textureset file.
rules.predicate: Resolve the path (the loader prefixes 'textureset\\' when absent; match the basename case-insensitively). The file must contain a TextureCount line AND at least one 'Start Texture%03d' block. A file with neither is not a textureset.
rules.fix: Point TextureSet at a real palette file.
rules.corpus: 6 of 177 .txt files in pack/textureset/textureset are not texturesets: metin2_siege_01/02/03.txt and their snow_ twins are pack manifests (FolderName "pack_map", List ExcludedFolderNameList { ... }). A tool that assumes 'it lives in textureset/ so it is one' parses zero entries and remaps every tile to 0.

rules.symptom: A ground texture tiles at an obviously wrong scale after a merge or reskin.
rules.checks: One texture path resolving to more than one UV scale in the union.
rules.predicate: After building the merged union, flag any texture path that appeared in two source sets with different (UScale, VScale). Dedup collapsed them to one entry and one source map now tiles differently.
rules.fix: Dedup on (path, uscale, vscale, uoffset, voffset) instead of path alone, or accept the warning. Render scale is fTerrainTexCoordBase * UScale with fTerrainTexCoordBase = 1/(16*200).
rules.corpus: Not measured across all pairs; the mechanism is documented in client-global-refs.md and MapForge's keyOf dedups on path only.

rules.symptom: Textures beyond slot 255 are unpaintable and unreachable after a merge.
rules.checks: Merged union size against the hard 255 ceiling.
rules.predicate: union.length <= 255. MAXTERRAINTEXTURES is 256 = 255 usable + the slot-0 eraser, and a tile.raw byte cannot exceed 255 anyway.
rules.fix: Drop unused textures before merging: scan each source's tile.raw for the indices actually painted and include only those in the union.
rules.corpus: MapForge only WARNS here and still writes the file (index.html:996). Treat as an error in m2map — slots 256+ are silently unpaintable.

rules.symptom: The sector has no collision at all; on the server an entire 4x4 block of server sectors is walkable.
rules.checks: attr.atr header and size.
rules.predicate: size == 65542 AND u16le[0] == 2634 AND u16le[1] == 256 AND u16le[2] == 256. Unlike height/tile this file IS validated on load and rejected outright.
rules.fix: Rewrite the 6-byte header before the 65536-byte payload.
rules.corpus: 0 violations in 1343 sectors.
rules.generator_note: MapForge's attrGrid() returns null on this check and generateServerAttr then writes attribute 0 for that sector — a silent size error becomes walk-through-the-world on the server.

rules.symptom: Player swims in mid-air, or cannot run across ground that looks dry.
rules.checks: attr WATER bit set where water.wtr has no water cell.
rules.predicate: For attr cell (ax, ay): if attr[ay*256+ax] & 0x02 then water.cells[(ay>>1)*128 + (ax>>1)] != 0xFF. Report the count per sector.
rules.fix: Clear the 0x02 bit where no water cell covers it, or add the water cell.
rules.corpus: 16 sectors violate this. Worst: metin2_map_duel/000000 (2611 cells), metin2_map_dawnmist_dungeon_01/000002 (51), metin2_map_b3/001002 (33).

rules.symptom: Player is blocked in open ground, or walks through a wall — client and server disagree about collision.
rules.checks: server_attr is a current regeneration of the attr.atr files.
rules.predicate: Regenerate server_attr in memory from the current attr.atr set and diff block by block; any differing block is a stale-generation hit. Cheap proxy: mtime(server_attr) > max(mtime(attr.atr)).
rules.fix: Regenerate. Recipe: for server sector (sx,sy) take client sectree (sx>>2, sy>>2), offset ((sx&3)*64, (sy&3)*64) into its 256x256 grid, mask each attr byte to & 0x07, copy into a uint32, upsample 2x2 into a 128x128 uint32 grid, LZO1X-compress, prefix uint32 size. Iterate y-major. MASK TO 0x07 -- ServerAttrGenerator.cpp and MapForge both copy the whole byte and both disagree with Ymir's shipped files; the whole-byte copy server-blocks the entire map (see ATR-004).
rules.corpus: No map under the corpus dir ships server_attr (it is a server-side file), so this is always a generation step for a deployed map. Six real ones sit beside their map folders on D:/ (map_a2, map_n_snowm_01, metin2_map_c1, metin2_map_n_flame_01, metin2_map_n_snow_dungeon_01, metin2_map_privatewar) and are the ground truth: from_attr_maps with the 0x07 default reproduces D:/map_a2/server_attr byte-for-byte across all 576 blocks. MapForge drops server_attr on merge and its status line ends 'regenerate server_attr before use'.

rules.symptom: Every cell of the map is impassable on the server, while the client shows open ground.
rules.checks: server_attr carries only the engine bits (0..2); paint bits never reach it.
rules.predicate: No server_attr DWORD may exceed 0x07. Equivalently, to_attr_grid(cx,cy).max() <= 0x07 for every sectree. The server blocks movement on ATTR_BLOCK|ATTR_OBJECT (0x01|0x80, char.cpp:5648, sectree_manager.cpp:823) and Ymir's paint puts bit 7 on WALKABLE mountain ground (0xC8), so any DWORD with bit 7 set is a cell the client draws as open and the server refuses to enter.
rules.fix: Mask to & 0x07 when generating server_attr. Keep the high bits in attr.atr itself -- the editor's paint conventions live there -- but never propagate them to the server file.
rules.corpus: Measured on map_a2: the whole-byte copy blocks 9,437,184 of 9,437,184 server cells; the shipped file blocks 6,246,724, which mask=0x07 reproduces exactly. 17 maps carry 0x80 on 100% of their cells (map_a2, map_n_snowm_01, map_n_threeway, guild_war1, guild_war2, metin2_map_a3, metin2_map_c3, guild_01, guild_03, monkeydungeon x3, t1-t4, trent) and are bricked outright by an unmasked copy. Paint values: 0x40 land walkable, 0x41 building blocked, 0xC8 mountain WALKABLE, 0xC9 mountain blocked -- bit 0 already carries the real collision, bit 7 only says 'this is mountain'.
rules.revision_note: Corrected 2026-09-08. This rule previously asserted the OPPOSITE -- that bit 7 must survive into server_attr and that masking causes walk-through buildings. That was wrong in the dangerous direction: it would have passed bricked maps and flagged correct ones.

rules.symptom: Paint information is lost after a rewrite; the editor's attribute overlay changes.
rules.checks: attr.atr high bits preserved when rewriting the CLIENT file.
rules.predicate: The byte-value histogram of a rewritten attr.atr must be a superset of the original's. This governs attr.atr only -- it is NOT a statement about server_attr, which must be masked to 0x07 (see ATR-004).
rules.fix: When adding a flag, OR it in; do not mask the client file.
rules.corpus: 36 distinct attr byte values across the corpus, max 205: {0-9,12,13,16,17,48-51,64,68,69,80,81,83,112,113,115,192-195,200-205}. Bit 7 appears ONLY in the 0xC0 family (192-195, 200-205), never as bare 0x80.

rules.symptom: Water renders at the wrong height — a lake floating above the valley, or a river sunk out of sight.
rules.checks: Water layer heights are raw height units, in the sector's plausible band.
rules.predicate: For each layer height h: 0 <= h <= 65535 AND min(height.raw) - 4000 <= h <= max(height.raw) + 4000. worldZ = h * HeightScale (0.5), the same scale as height.raw — writing centimetres instead of raw units doubles every water plane.
rules.fix: Store raw units, not cm.
rules.corpus: 0 out-of-range heights in 1343 sectors.

rules.symptom: Water planes at nonsense elevations in this engine, even though the file 'parses'.
rules.checks: Legacy 2-byte height array.
rules.predicate: rest = size - 16391. Flag when rest == 2*N and N > 0. The loader recognises the legacy layout, converts the WORDs, then falls through and unconditionally re-copies 4*N bytes from the same offset (Terrain.cpp:286-292), overwriting the converted values with misread data.
rules.fix: Always write the 4-byte int32 form: 7 + 16384 + 4*N bytes.
rules.corpus: 0 legacy files in 142 maps — every shipped water.wtr is the 4-byte form. Keep the check; converters still produce them.

rules.symptom: A water plane at a random elevation, or water that does not render.
rules.checks: water.wtr header, size formula, and cell index range.
rules.predicate: u16le[0] == 5426 AND u16le[1] == 128 AND u16le[2] == 128 AND size == 16391 + 4*N (N = byte at offset 6) AND for every one of the 16384 cells: cell == 0xFF OR cell < N.
rules.fix: Rewrite out-of-range indices as 0xFF (dry).
rules.corpus: 0 violations. Also 0 sectors with duplicate layer heights, so a global height->id reindex is a total function in practice. Layer counts: 0 in 848 sectors, 1 in 320, 2 in 100, 3 in 38, max 17.

rules.symptom: Player walks on the water surface instead of swimming, or drowns with no water visible.
rules.checks: Every VISIBLE water cell carries the ATTRIBUTE_WATER (0x02) bit.
rules.predicate: MUST be height-aware. For water cell (cx,cy): v = cells[cy*128+cx]; skip if v == 0xFF or v >= N; terrain = height.raw[(cy+1)*131 + (cx+1)]; if heights[v] > terrain then assert any(attr[(cy*2+dy)*256 + (cx*2+dx)] & 0x02 for dy in (0,1) for dx in (0,1)).
rules.fix: Recompute the 0x02 bit from this predicate and OR it into the existing attr byte. Do not mask attr.atr itself -- its paint bits must survive. This is distinct from M2MAP-ATR-004, which masks on the way OUT to server_attr.
rules.corpus: The naive rule ('every non-0xFF cell must be flagged') fires on 452 of 1343 sectors and is unusable — a water cell only means 'inside a brush footprint', and water below terrain is correctly left unflagged. Height-aware measurements: map_a2/000000 (1 layer) 606 cells above terrain, 1677 below, 0 unflagged. metin2_map_duel/000000 (1 layer) 2749 above, 3689 below, 0 unflagged. metin2_map_b3/001002 (8 layers) 3190 above, 3378 below, 566 unflagged — a genuine defect the naive rule could not isolate.

rules.symptom: Shadows absent, or character shading disagrees with the shadows baked into the ground.
rules.checks: shadowmap.raw size and .dds/.raw pairing.
rules.predicate: If shadowmap.raw exists its size must be exactly 131072 (this one IS strictly validated on load and rejected otherwise). .dds and .raw should both be present or both absent — the client renders terrain from the .dds and samples point shadow colour from the .raw.
rules.fix: Regenerate both together, or delete both (missing is non-fatal; terrain renders unshadowed). Encoding is RGB555: b=(t&0x1f)<<3, g=((t>>5)&0x1f)<<3, r=((t>>10)&0x1f)<<3, despite an in-source comment claiming R5G6B5. Row 0 is the north edge.
rules.corpus: 1336 of 1336 shadowmap.raw are exactly 131072 — perfect conformance. 7 sectors have no shadowmap.raw, 11 have no shadowmap.dds.

rules.symptom: Minimap tile blank, or a DDS reader rejects official map data.
rules.checks: minimap.dds / shadowmap.dds presence and header-driven format parse.
rules.predicate: NEVER check by size. Magic 'DDS ' at 0, height at 12, width at 16, mipcount at 28, pixel-format flags at 80, FourCC at 84, bpp at 88. Accept DXT1/DXT3/DXT5 and uncompressed alike.
rules.fix: Header-driven parse; treat a missing file as non-fatal.
rules.corpus: THE SPEC IS WRONG HERE — measurement wins. mapformat/minimap-dds.md and shadowmap.md call 262272 bytes (uncompressed X8R8G8B8 256x256) 'typical'. Not ONE file in 1332 sectors is that size. Actual: minimap.dds 32896 x1270 (DXT1 256x256, 0 mips) and 43832 x62 (DXT1, 9 mips); shadowmap.dds 43832 x1328, 32896 x1, 87536 x2 (DXT5), 262271 x1 (uncompressed 24bpp, metin2_map_capedragonhead/005003). 32896 = 128 header + 8 bytes/block * 4096 blocks. 11 sectors have no minimap.dds.

rules.symptom: A placed object simply is not there in-game. No error, no placeholder.
rules.checks: Every areadata CRC resolves to a registered property.
rules.predicate: Build {crc -> property} by scanning property/: require FourCC 'YPRT' at offset 0 and \r\n at offset 4; the CRC is line 0 of the body as decimal ASCII, read VERBATIM — never recomputed from the filename. Then assert every areadata token[3] is in that set. CPropertyManager::Get(crc) misses are dropped silently at load.
rules.fix: Ship the property, or remove the record.
rules.corpus: 2112 CRCs from 2605 files under property/ — 492 files are .gr2/.mdatr art and the 'reserve' list living inside the property tree; skip anything without the FourCC. One duplicate CRC 1740984444 claimed by devils_dragon_island/mtthunder_thorn01.prb and devils_dragon_island/thing/obj_mtthund_thorn01.prb; registration is last-one-wins.

rules.symptom: A strict parser throws on an official map's CRC field.
rules.checks: CRC token carrying a non-vanilla '#scale#scale#scale' suffix.
rules.predicate: Parse the CRC the way atoi does: int(re.match(r'-?\d+', token).group()) in Python, or parseInt(token, 10) in JS (which already truncates at the '#'). Do not require the token to be a bare integer.
rules.fix: Truncate at the first non-digit. Preserve the suffix on round-trip if you want to keep the scale.
rules.corpus: All 288 object records in metin2_map_treasure_hunt use '<crc>#<sx>#<sy>#<sz>', e.g. '142625613#1.000000#1.000000#1.000000'. The vanilla engine reads them fine via atoi. All 288 resolve after stripping (193 Building, 95 Tree). Python int() and radix-checked parses throw.

rules.symptom: One object per sector silently vanishes; occasionally a whole sector's objects.
rules.checks: ObjectCount agrees with the Object%03d blocks actually present, and appears exactly once.
rules.predicate: blocks = parse_start_end(text) with lowercased keys; declared = int(blocks['objectcount'][0]); present = {k for k in blocks if k.startswith('object') and k != 'objectcount'}; assert len(present) == declared AND all f'object{i:03d}' in present for i in range(declared) AND text.lower().count('objectcount') == 1. The k != 'objectcount' exclusion is mandatory — 'objectcount' itself starts with 'object' and produces a universal off-by-one without it.
rules.fix: Renumber Object000..ObjectN-1 contiguously and write a single trailing ObjectCount.
rules.corpus: 7 sectors of metin2_map_t1 are corrupt in shipped data (000000, 000001, 001000, 001001, 001002, 002000, 002002): the 'Start Object000' line was overwritten with 'ObjectCount 0', so object000's tokens leak into the top-level namespace and the file carries two ObjectCount keys. One object is lost per sector; in 002002 that is the only object.

rules.symptom: Objects pop in and out as the player walks, at a boundary unrelated to where they stand.
rules.checks: Object position lies inside the sector whose folder lists it.
rules.predicate: Coordinates are map-local cm and y is stored NEGATED. For sector (ax, ay): ax*25600 <= x <= (ax+1)*25600 AND ay*25600 <= -y <= (ay+1)*25600. Report the overshoot in cm; the client only loads a 3x3 sectree window (AROUND_AREA_NUM), so a far-out object exists only while its listing sector is in that window.
rules.fix: Move the record into the folder that geometrically contains it.
rules.corpus: 553 of 48851 records sit outside their own sector. Median overshoot 5900 cm, p90 79848 cm, max 101801 cm (four sectors away). Only 114 are within 1000 cm (the legitimate 'big building straddling the border' case); 407 within 12800 cm. Suggested thresholds: <= 1280 cm info, > 1280 cm minor, > 25600 cm major. Worst: map_n_snowm_01/002005 (y = -127610 in a sector spanning -128000..-153600).

rules.symptom: Object buried in the ground, or floating above it.
rules.checks: Final object Z against sampled terrain height.
rules.predicate: finalZ = token[2] + token[5]; terrainZ = height.raw[(vy+1)*131 + (vx+1)] * HeightScale sampled at (x, -y) (bilinear across the cell's two triangles, split on xdist <= ydist; nearest-vertex is fine for an audit); flag |finalZ - terrainZ| > 2000 cm. Separately flag |token[5]| > 2000 cm as a weaker signal.
rules.fix: Recompute Z from terrain * HeightScale, not from raw units.
rules.corpus: 120 records carry |bias| > 2000 cm legitimately (metin2_12zi_stage/001003 object002 bias=4987; metin2_map_dawnmist_dungeon_01/001000 object023 bias=-3000) — large biases are how Ymir sinks pillars and raises platforms. Bias alone is minor; combine with the terrain delta before escalating.

rules.symptom: Object rotated by roughly a tenth of the intended angle, or not rotated at all.
rules.checks: Rotation token shape.
rules.predicate: token[4] matches ^-?\d+\.\d{6}#-?\d+\.\d{6}#-?\d+\.\d{6}$. Flag any token[4] without a '#'. Two engine defects compound: yaw is extracted with substr(0, s-1), dropping the character before the first '#' (Area.cpp:850) — harmless for %f values ('120.000000' -> '120.00000') but destructive for bare integers ('90#0#0' -> yaw 9); and a token with no '#' is read as ROLL only (legacy shape).
rules.fix: Always write the three-part %f form, e.g. 0.000000#0.000000#120.000000.
rules.corpus: 0 bare-integer rotations in 48851 records — every shipped record uses %f#%f#%f. Entirely a generator hazard.

rules.symptom: areadata record parses but the object type is nonsense (an ambience emitter placed as scenery).
rules.checks: Resolved property type is scenery, not ambience.
rules.predicate: Resolved PropertyType in {Tree, Building, Effect, DungeonBlock}. An Ambience property here loads and dispatches, but the record has no range field so the emitter gets range 0 and is silent.
rules.fix: Move ambience records to areaambiencedata.txt.
rules.corpus: 48851 records: Building 22871, Tree 14239, Effect 8121, DungeonBlock 3332, Ambience 0 (excluding the 288 treasure_hunt records with the '#scale' CRC form). The separation holds perfectly in shipped data.

rules.symptom: Ambient sound never plays, or plays at a nonsense radius.
rules.checks: areaambiencedata schema — which is NOT the areadata schema.
rules.predicate: Header 'AreaAmbienceDataFile'; >= 5 tokens per record; token[3] resolves to a property whose PropertyType is 'Ambience'; token[4] is an integer > 0 (audible radius in cm, read unconditionally — 0 disables); token[5] if present is a float 0..1. In areadata token 4 is ROTATION; in areaambiencedata it is RANGE. Mixing the two schemas corrupts records silently.
rules.fix: Write range in cm, not a rotation string.
rules.corpus: 28 ambience records total, all exactly 6 tokens, all resolving to Ambience properties, none with range 0.

rules.symptom: A building renders but has no collision — the player walks straight through it.
rules.checks: The .mdatr collision mesh derived from a Building/DungeonBlock property exists.
rules.predicate: For each .prb/.prd, read BuildingFile/DungeonBlockFile, map 'd:\\ymir work\\...' onto the extracted art root, and test that the same path with extension .mdatr exists.
rules.fix: Do not rely on object collision. Paint the 0xC0-family bytes into attr.atr under building footprints — which is exactly what official maps do.
rules.corpus: 183 of 400 sampled .prb files have NO .mdatr on disk (e.g. D:\ymir work\zone\12temple\12t_12statue_01.mdatr). Nearly half the building catalogue carries no derived collision. A generator that places buildings and expects collision to appear by itself produces walk-through buildings.

rules.symptom: Fog, lighting and sky fall back to engine defaults; the map looks flat and grey.
rules.checks: The setting.txt Environment reference resolves.
rules.predicate: Resolution order: <mapdir>\<name>, then d:/ymir work/environment/<name>, then a fallback on the last two characters of the map name. Assert one of them exists.
rules.fix: Ship the .msenv or point at an existing one. Defaults when keys are absent: fog 12800/17920, skybox scale 3500^3, cloud scale 200000^2, cloud height 30000.
rules.corpus: 121 .msenv in the pack; 0 unresolved references across all 142 maps.

rules.symptom: The server aborts map loading entirely — every map fails, not just the broken one.
rules.checks: Case-exact Setting.txt and Town.txt for every map listed in index.
rules.predicate: For every non-comment line of index ('<int> <folder>', // and # are comments), the folder must contain files named exactly 'Setting.txt' and exactly 'Town.txt'. Compare against os.listdir byte-for-byte, not case-insensitively — the server usually runs on a case-sensitive filesystem. SECTREE_MANAGER::Build returns failure on the first miss and the whole pass dies.
rules.fix: Ship Setting.txt and Town.txt capitalised; server_attr, regen.txt, npc.txt, boss.txt, stone.txt, dungeon.txt lowercase.
rules.corpus: Not measurable from a client corpus (0 of 142 maps carry server files). Purely a deployment check.

rules.symptom: Every wall and building is walkable on the server while looking solid on the client.
rules.checks: server_attr exists, its dimensions match, and every block decompresses to 65536 bytes.
rules.predicate: int32 W at 0, int32 H at 4; assert W == MapSizeX*4 AND H == MapSizeY*4. Then walk W*H blocks of (uint32 size + size bytes) in Y-MAJOR order (for y: for x:) and assert the offset chain lands exactly on EOF and each block LZO1X-decompresses to exactly 65536 bytes. LoadAttribute bails on a size mismatch but Build IGNORES that failure and continues (sectree_manager.cpp:789-790), so the map boots with missing attributes rather than refusing.
rules.fix: Regenerate (see M2MAP-ATR-003). LZO1X, not zlib — worst-case compressed bound n + (n>>4) + 67.
rules.corpus: 0 of 142 client maps ship server_attr; expected for an extracted client map, fatal for a deployment.

rules.symptom: Player spawns in the void, or under the terrain.
rules.checks: Town.txt coordinates land on real terrain.
rules.predicate: Coordinates are map-local units of 100 (world = Base + value*100). Assert 0 <= townX <= MapSizeX*256 AND 0 <= townY <= MapSizeY*256; the covering sector folder must exist; terrain height there must be non-zero. If the optional 6 per-empire ints are present, ALL SIX must be — the server ignores a partial set. NOTE: dungeon.txt uses raw world units with NO x100 scaling — do not apply this predicate to it.
rules.fix: Recompute Town.txt after any resize or merge.
rules.corpus: Not measurable from a client corpus.

rules.symptom: A regen line never spawns anything — not even once at boot.
rules.checks: The time column carries an s/m/h suffix and is non-zero.
rules.predicate: Column 7 matches ^(\d+[smh])+$ and evaluates non-zero. Digits without a suffix are DISCARDED by the parser (regen.cpp:187-217) so '60' becomes 0, and time == 0 disables the line completely — not even the initial spawn happens (regen.cpp:766).
rules.fix: Normalise to Ns/Nm/Nh on save; '1m' is conventional.
rules.corpus: 1073 regen lines across all four file types in all 142 maps: 0 bare-digit times. Generator hazard only.

rules.symptom: A group spawn line spawns nothing, or one wrong mob.
rules.checks: g/ga/r lines have non-zero half-extents.
rules.predicate: if line_type[0] in 'gr': assert (sx, sy) != (0, 0). The dispatcher tests sx==ex && sy==ey BEFORE the type switch (regen.cpp:417); a degenerate rect takes the point path, which calls SpawnMob with the group id as if it were a mob vnum.
rules.fix: Give group lines a non-zero range.
rules.corpus: 1073 lines, types r=668 g=361 m=44, all 11 columns: 0 point-spawn traps. Generator hazard only.

rules.symptom: Spawns land outside the map, or in the wrong quadrant after a merge.
rules.checks: Regen coordinates are in range for the map size after any shift.
rules.predicate: 0 <= cx <= MapSizeX*256 AND 0 <= cy <= MapSizeY*256. Columns are in units of 100 world-units (metres); one sectree = 25600 cm = 256 regen units. sx/sy are HALF-EXTENTS around the centre, not start coordinates. World rect: sx_world = (cx - sxHalf)*100 + BaseX, ey_world = (cy + syHalf)*100 + BaseY.
rules.fix: On merge, shift by whole sectors: cx += (quadrantOffsetX - sourceMinX) * 256. 'e' (exception) rows get the x100 scaling but NOT the base offset and end after column 5, so a column-count-strict parser must special-case them. Column 8 'percent' is parsed and discarded (regen.cpp:222-224) — keep writing 100 for byte-compat.
rules.corpus: All 1073 shipped regen lines carry 11 columns; no 'e' rows in the corpus.

rules.symptom: Merged map has one half at double or half elevation, or the server's geometry does not match the client's.
rules.checks: All merge inputs share CellScale and HeightScale.
rules.predicate: For every input slot: cellScale == primary.cellScale AND heightScale == primary.heightScale. The merged map gets ONE setting.txt, and every height.raw is copied verbatim, so its raw values get reinterpreted under the survivor's HeightScale. CellScale is worse: the client hard-codes 200 but the server multiplies map dimensions by the file value (sectree_manager.cpp:262,276).
rules.fix: Refuse the merge. Compare with parseFloat and an epsilon, then normalise the output to CellScale 200 / HeightScale 0.500000. MapForge compares String(...) on both sides, so 0.5 vs 0.500000 fails the gate — over-strict but safe.
rules.corpus: Every one of the 139 maps with a setting.txt uses CellScale 200 and HeightScale 0.500000. The gate never fires on official data; it exists for community maps.

rules.symptom: Merge silently produces a map with the wrong ground textures everywhere.
rules.checks: Every merge input has a resolvable TextureSet before the merge starts.
rules.predicate: findTextureSetFile resolves for EVERY slot: an explicitly attached file, else a file whose basename matches setting.txt's TextureSet value, else any textureset*.txt in the drop. Null for any slot must abort the merge and name the slots (TL/TR/BL/BR) that need one.
rules.fix: Refuse and ask. The TextureSet lives OUTSIDE the map folder so a dragged map folder usually does not contain it, and merging without it is not degradable — you either leave the tile indices wrong or lose the palette.
rules.corpus: MapForge's error path: 'attach a textureset .txt for: <slots> (needed to remap tiles + rewrite the TextureSet field)'.

rules.symptom: After a merge or reskin, ground textures are scrambled or shifted by one slot.
rules.checks: The tile-index remap is derived from parsed block numbers and seeds the eraser.
rules.predicate: The remap must satisfy: remap[0] == 0 (slot 0 is the built-in eraser, excluded from TextureCount); union slots are 1-BASED; the source slot key is the block's parsed Texture%03d NUMBER, not its position in the file; the remap is applied to ALL 66564 bytes including the 1-tile border skirt; an index with no remap entry maps to 0 and is reported, never passed through.
rules.fix: Dedup the union on the lowercased forward-slashed texture path so shared ground textures collapse to one slot. Emit a dense Texture001..TextureN run.
rules.corpus: MapForge uses idx+1 (file position) as the source slot, which breaks on metin2_guild_village.txt (slot 1 missing) and metin2_BayBlackSand.txt (slot 3 missing) — every tile after the hole remaps one texture off. MapForge also passes unmapped indices through unchanged, which matters for the 47 sectors that index past their own TextureCount.

rules.symptom: Water renders at another sector's elevation in 3D tools after a merge.
rules.checks: Global water-layer reindex is correct, or is correctly abandoned.
rules.predicate: Pass 1 collects distinct heights across ALL sectors of ALL inputs, skipping cells where v == 0xFF or v >= heights.length. Pass 2 rewrites each sector's cells as (v == 0xFF or v >= heights.length) ? 0xFF : globalId[heights[v]], with the global height array. Guard: if the global table exceeds 255 distinct heights, ABANDON normalisation entirely and leave every sector's water untouched — NumWater is a single uint8 at offset 6, so 256 would write 0 and put every cell out of range. Always serialise the 4-byte int32 form.
rules.fix: Degrade, do not corrupt. Log out-of-range indices healed to 0xFF.
rules.corpus: Max layers in any shipped sector is 17 and no sector has duplicate layer heights, so the height->id mapping is total and a 4-quadrant union stays far under 255 in practice.

rules.symptom: After a merge, objects are mirrored across the map's horizontal axis, or spawns are one sector off.
rules.checks: The three coordinate shifts use their three different units, and areadata Y is SUBTRACTED.
rules.predicate: Sector folder: nx = (srcX - srcMinX) + quadOffX, name = pad3(nx)+pad3(ny). Regen: cx += (quadOffX - srcMinX) * 256 (256 regen units per sector). Areadata: x += (quadOffX - srcMinX) * 25600 AND y -= (quadOffY - srcMinY) * 25600 — MINUS, because areadata y is stored negated.
rules.fix: The 'y -= ' line is the single easiest thing to get wrong in a merge and it fails silently. Assert after the shift that every object still satisfies M2MAP-ARD-004 for its new folder.
rules.corpus: MapForge index.html:1004-1030. Quadrant layout: col0 = max(w_TL, w_BL), col1 = max(w_TR, w_BR), row0 = max(h_TL, h_TR), row1 = max(h_BL, h_BR); off = [[0,0],[col0,0],[0,row0],[col0,row0]]; totalW = col0+col1.

rules.symptom: A merged or reskinned map ships with stale derived artefacts.
rules.checks: The four artefacts that are stale by construction after any merge or reskin.
rules.predicate: After a merge/reskin, assert: (1) server_attr regenerated (M2MAP-ATR-003); (2) height skirts re-stitched at every NEW internal seam (M2MAP-HGT-002) — height.raw is copied verbatim so new quadrant boundaries are unstitched; (3) the minimap atlas rebuilt from the per-sector minimap.dds; (4) atlasinfo.txt updated to the new MapSize and BasePosition (M2MAP-SET-004).
rules.fix: Run all four as a post-merge stage. MapForge's own status line is the checklist: 'merged N maps -> WxH · water: K global layers · regenerate server_attr before use'.
rules.corpus: MapForge index.html:1032-1046. Everything except tile.raw, water.wtr, areadata.txt and server_attr is copied byte-for-byte into the renamed folder — correct, since none of those files contain coordinates, but it is exactly why the four artefacts above go stale.

rules.symptom: A dropped folder produces an empty merge slot, or a merge that silently drops a whole map.
rules.checks: Each merge input actually contains XXXYYY sector folders.
rules.predicate: After stripping a common path prefix, collect sector ids with /^(\d{6})\//. Refuse the slot when the set is empty: 'that folder has no XXXYYY sectors'. This catches the two most common drops — the parent of the map folder, and a map whose sector folders are named anything but six digits.
rules.fix: Fail fast with that message. Then take dimensions from setting.txt when present and infer them from the sector bounds otherwise (w = mapSizeX || maxx-minx+1), and keep each slot's own minx/miny for the offset math — that is what makes an origin-offset map like metin2_map_smhgate_b1 (sectors starting at x=2) mergeable at all.
rules.corpus: 26 of 142 corpus maps would hit this guard: they contain only mapproperty.txt (± setting.txt) and zero sector folders.
